propositions: Parallel multi-session writes to the git-backed tickets store cause wedging when compaction mutations to the worktree (snapshot writes, retired renames, archived deletions) precede their git commit with no rollback on worker death, leaving dirty trees that break sync and push operations.

The union_merge sync operation aborts in two classes: untracked files that origin wants to create, and tracked-file deletions/modifications; unhandled tracked-file cases strand local ticket commits off origin and fail plan-review/close attestations due to strict git status checks.

Runtime markers (*/.archived, */.write.lock) committed before their gitignore patterns were added remain tracked in HEAD, causing perpetual marker churn to appear as tracked dirt and blocking every merge.

Compaction must become crash-atomic with rollback parity: an intent journal outside the worktree records fold intent before any mutation, recovery reverts incomplete folds via this journal on next sweep or doctor run, and the journal is cleared only after commit success or intentional retention for snapshot repair.
Both reconverge and push-recovery paths must recover from tracked-artifact deletions/modifications and untracked-collision aborts, retrying the merge once with artifacts restored or quarantined.
Store-wide scans (fsck, compact-all) must default to active tickets only and accept --include-archived to include archived tickets, so scan cost scales with the active working set.
